learnerStatement: Simulated learner. This review finds problems; it is not evidence that anyone learned.
learnerBoundary: Everyday numeracy, simple charts, comparing numbers and familiar household objects; no domain-specific theory assumed.

observations.prediction: Selected 12.5 years and locked the doubling prediction for 8% annual compounding. The initial disabled chart and slider showed 7%, while the question used 8%.
observations.exploration: Set 8%: exact doubling 9.0 years, shortcut 9.0, simple interest 12.5. Then tried 4%: exact 17.7, shortcut 18.0, simple 25.0. Finally tried 20%: exact 3.8, shortcut 3.6, simple 5.0.
observations.reveal: The reveal corrected the answer to 9 years and explained interest earning interest. It stated the 72 divided by rate shortcut and a 5% to 20% accuracy range. It called 20% the rate I tried next, although I actually tried 4% between 8% and 20%; the numeric comparison itself matched the last state.
observations.visual: Inspected the inline dark 1257 by 936 screenshot at 8%. Bars pulled above a dashed simple interest line and crossed a horizontal 200 line at a labelled 9.0 years. Exact, shortcut and simple readouts were legible beneath.
observations.isolation: No-history evaluation preview banner present. Visible trust count ignored.
observations.reference: Own CUA tab 543884163 snapshots and inspected inline screenshot; no screenshot file saved.

prediction.reason: The options distinguish simple from compounded growth.
prediction.evidence: Selected the 12.5 year simple interest result for an 8% compound question.

interaction.reason: Changing rates compares an approximation with exact growth and simple interest.
interaction.evidence: 8%, 4% and 20% showed both agreement and approximation error.

payoff.reason: The mechanism is explained, but the personalized sequence description is inaccurate.
payoff.evidence: The reveal says 20% was tried next despite the intervening 4% trial.

clarity.reason: The chart clearly contrasts the two growth mechanisms, with a small initial rate mismatch.
clarity.evidence: The prediction asks 8% while the initial chart shows 7%; the prompt directs setting 8%.

transfer.reason: The shortcut is actionable with a stated range of accuracy.
transfer.evidence: 72 divided by rate is compared at multiple rates and qualified for 5% to 20%.

accessibility.evidence: Keyboard, focus, contrast audit, phone, zoom/reflow and motion unknown.

surprise.reason: Interest on interest shortens doubling substantially.
surprise.evidence: 8% compounded doubled in 9 years rather than 12.5.

visualExplanation.reason: The bars pulling away from the straight dashed path explain acceleration.
visualExplanation.evidence: The compound path reaches the 200 line earlier.

playfulness.reason: One rate slider supports quick comparisons.

practicalValue.reason: The shortcut supports quick growth estimates.
practicalValue.evidence: The reveal gives a usable rule and an error range.

depth.reason: The lesson distinguishes the mechanism from an approximate rule.
depth.evidence: Exact doubling, simple doubling and shortcut are shown together.

complexity.reason: Compounding and approximation require more than simple percentages, but the comparison has one control.
complexity.conceptualDemand: Moderate: growth applies to accumulated growth as well as the starting amount.
complexity.conceptualChallenge: Distinguish constant additions from repeated multiplication.
complexity.prerequisiteNovelty: Compound growth and approximate doubling rules are introduced.
complexity.notationRepresentationBurden: Moderate: bars, reference line, repeated multiplication and several time readouts.

whyCool: A curved growth path turns a simple division trick into a surprisingly close estimate.
caveat: The reveal misstates the order of my rate trials. Constant annual growth is assumed, and the initial chart rate differs from the prediction rate.
missingEvidence: No varying annual rate sequence was tested.
